text: Not enough leads coming in. You refresh the inbox, and there's nothing new.
So you try emailing new companies. It usually goes wrong in four places.
One. Nobody has the time for it.
Two. Your emails land in spam, and nobody tells you.
Three. The list is old, so emails bounce back or reach the wrong person.
Four. Replies wait for days, and people who said not now are forgotten.
So we take the whole job off your hands. It's called the Managed Outbound Channel.
We find the right companies, write to them, follow up, answer the replies, and book the meetings into your calendar.
Step one. We agree who you want as customers. Each campaign gets one goal, like reaching new companies, reviving old leads, or finding more like your best customers.
Step two. We set up separate inboxes on web addresses like yours, so your main email stays safe.
Each is set up so Gmail knows it's you, then warmed up for three weeks, on an account used only for you.
How much we send depends on what you need, from 18,000 emails a month up to 80,000 or more.
Step three. We search wide. Then an AI agent reads each company's website, to check it's the kind you want, before we look anyone up.
Step four. We watch for a reason to write, like a new hire, funding or a tender, so each first email opens with a line meant only for them.
Step five. Every address is checked, down to whether the person still works there.
If more than two in a hundred would bounce, that list isn't sent.
Step six. Three short emails in one week, the third with a new angle. Then we stop, or move to LinkedIn for the ones worth it.
We test the wording one change at a time: subject lines, opening lines, and what we ask them to do.
Then someone replies.
Step seven. Within a minute, an AI agent reads the reply and sorts it: interested, a question, not now, or an out-of-office.
It's answered your way: book them straight in, ask your questions first, or hand them to your team.
At first, a person approves every reply. Quotes and contracts always go to your team.
Step eight. The conversation carries on by email, LinkedIn, a call, or WhatsApp once they've agreed.
Our research travels with them, so a brief is ready before the meeting: who they are, why we wrote, and what to ask.
And your CRM, where you keep track of customers, fills itself in.
Step nine. Meetings get booked, confirmed and reminded, and no-shows get followed up.
If someone says not now, we note why and set a date, and the follow-up goes out by itself.
Every month, one report: meetings held, qualified conversations, how many replied, and what each meeting cost.
Qualified means they fit, they're interested, and they've confirmed a meeting.
We don't track opens. That needs a hidden tracker in every email, and spam filters count it against you.
We do our own outreach too. Since August, nearly 3,000 emails, 9 qualified conversations, and 7 demos booked.
One company ignored our first two emails. The third got a reply in 55 minutes, then a call, then a demo booked.
And the channel is sending by week four. A new sales hire usually takes two to three months to get up to speed.
We'll never promise you a number of leads, replies or meetings. Judge us on whether the work is done properly, and whether anybody got lost.
Your part is small. Tell us who to reach, give us one hour on how you sell, and name who takes the meetings. Then approve once a month, and take the conversations.
It starts with a thirty-minute call. If it's a fit, you get a written plan within five working days, with the first ten companies we'd contact. Free, and yours to keep.
The Managed Outbound Channel, by Rheo AI. Book your call on this page.
